extracted_factors.Label: Political Turnover
extracted_factors.Description: Political changes, such as election cycles, impact the continuity and success of REDD+ initiatives by influencing laws and regulations.

extracted_factors.Label: Institutionalization of REDD+
extracted_factors.Description: Embedding REDD+ into national and regional laws and institutions is necessary for long-term sustainability and success.

extracted_factors.Label: Socioeconomic and Political Drivers of Deforestation
extracted_factors.Description: The focus on economic policy over environmental concerns influences deforestation rates, affecting REDD+ implementation.

extracted_factors.Label: Jurisdictional REDD+ Programs
extracted_factors.Description: Jurisdictional programs at the subnational level help focus on holistic forest and land-use strategies, but progress varies significantly across jurisdictions.

extracted_factors.Label: Private Sector Sustainability Initiatives
extracted_factors.Description: Initiatives like those in the palm oil sector provide potential support for REDD+, but face resistance from some government sectors.

extracted_factors.Label: Weak Law Enforcement
extracted_factors.Description: Insufficient law enforcement weakens efforts to protect forests and implement REDD+ strategies effectively.

extracted_factors.Label: Climate Change
extracted_factors.Description: Global climate challenges necessitate initiatives like REDD+ to be included in broader climate mitigation strategies.

extracted_factors.Label: Decentralization of Governance
extracted_factors.Description: Decentralization can empower local actors but also leads to challenges like corruption, impacting deforestation rates.
